newsitem.title: USA: Daschle said Republican U.S. tax cut too much.
newsitem.headline: Daschle said Republican U.S. tax cut too much.

text.p: Senate Democratic Leader Tom Daschle said Tuesday Republicans' proposal for a broad tax cut was "probably too much," telling reporters at a news conference, "I don't think they (Republicans) really expect to get something of that magnitude passed."
Senate Republicans Tuesday will introduce a bill calling for $163 billion in five-year tax cuts, including a capital gains reduction and $500 per child tax credit.

Assistant Republican Leader Don Nickles, an Oklahoma Republican, said his party's overall package of tax cuts could be close to $170 billion over five years when separate legislation, including new education tax breaks, is added in.
"We put the cost ... on the tax provision, I think it's about $170 billion over five years," Nickles said.

Senate Republicans Tuesday plan to introduce 10 bills laying out their priorities for the coming session. Among them is a $163 billion package of tax cuts, including a capital gains reduction and $500-per-child tax credit.

A package of educational initiatives will also be introduced, including investment accounts to help parents save for college costs; a change to make interest on student loans tax-deductible and new tax preferences for state pre-paid tuition plans, education plans provided by employers and student work-study awards.
Daschle, a South Dakota Democrat, warned that lawmakers had to be careful how deeply they cut taxes, especially if the primary goal was to balance the budget.
"We have to be very careful, very prudent about how we do this ... the real prospect of passing a bill of that magnitude is very difficult," Daschle said.
Daschle admitted Democrats did not have a cost estimate for a package of tax breaks they plan to introduce, including education tax cuts and a more narrow capital gains reduction.
